audit.why: 20% over 5 games. That is the smallest sample in my slice and nowhere near enough to carry a claim on its own, so I let the kit drive the analysis and did not lean on the number. The direction it points - Maokai ahead - is well supported independently.

audit.whatIsWrong: The mechanism behind the entire matchup is absent. Riot's Sap Magic text: 'Maokai's basic attack also heals him and deals additional damage on a moderate cooldown. Each time Maokai casts a spell OR IS STRUCK BY AN ENEMY'S SPELL, this cooldown is reduced.' Meanwhile Mel's Radiant Volley 'explodes around a target location, dealing damage repeatedly to enemies within the area'.
audit.why: Mel's primary poke is multi-hit, and every one of those hits shortens the cooldown on his heal. So her best tool in the lane is simultaneously the thing that refills him fastest. The entry already notices the symptom - 'the chip damage that should snowball just resets every wave' - but never gives the cause, so the reader has no way to reason about it. Knowing it changes the plan from 'poke more' to 'poke in bursts you can convert, or do not poke at all'.
audit.corrected: Sap Magic's heal cooldown falls every time a spell strikes him, and Radiant Volley ticks repeatedly.

audit.whatIsWrong: Twisted Advance makes Maokai untargetable and neither layer says so. Riot: 'Maokai contorts into a mass of moving roots, becoming untargetable and dashing to the target.' _missing-interactions.json flags it as untargetable-dodges-burst.
audit.why: Golden Eclipse strikes everyone carrying Overwhelm regardless of distance - it is Mel's payoff for a whole lane of stacking, on a 120s cooldown at rank 1. Fired into his W animation it finds no target. The entry tells the reader to detonate when he commits, which is exactly the moment he is untargetable.
audit.corrected: He is untargetable inside Twisted Advance - never spend the detonation into that window.

audit.whatIsWrong: whys[3] states 'his W is up far more often than your E'. Twisted Advance is 14/13/12/11/10. Mel's Solar Snare is 11/10.5/10/9.5/9. Her root is up MORE often than his dash at every single rank.
audit.why: It is backwards, and it is the reason the entry counsels hoarding. If the reader believes they are losing the cooldown war they play the root as a scarce emergency item and concede step-ups they could contest. The true picture - 11s against 14s - means Solar Snare can be held purely as anti-engage and still be available every time he dashes.
audit.corrected: Solar Snare at 11s beats Twisted Advance at 14s; the root cycles faster than the dash.

audit.whatIsWrong: content.mid says 'Your W barrier eats projectiles, but Maokai's threats are a dash and a melee knockback, not projectiles, so it gives you almost nothing here.' The projectile half is right - nothing in Maokai's kit carries the projectile flag - but the conclusion is wrong. Rebuttal also 'prevents her from taking damage, and grants her movement speed'.
audit.why: Damage prevention and a move-speed burst are precisely what an immobile mage wants against a targeted gap-close into melee. Writing the barrier off as worthless in the one matchup where she most needs to walk out of melee range is the opposite of the correct read. It also breaks the relevance rule by spending a sentence on a non-interaction.
audit.corrected: Say what Rebuttal does do here - blank his damage and take the move speed to walk out - rather than what it cannot reflect.
sources: champ-data/_kits/maokai.json (no projectile flag on any slot)

audit.whatIsWrong: Nature's Grasp is never mentioned anywhere in either layer. It is a 3000-range advancing wall of brambles that roots everything in its path, on 130/110/90.
audit.why: For a champion with no dash it is the escape-denial tool that decides whether a lost fight becomes a death. _missing-interactions.json flags it as terrain-cuts-retreat with the note to hold Flash for the wall rather than the damage, and that is the right instruction - it just was not anywhere in the entry.
audit.corrected: Added to the cooldown list and the late-game text: keep Flash for Nature's Grasp, not for the damage.

audit.whatIsWrong: Sustain is repeatedly credited to his saplings: 'his sapling sustain has already refilled the HP your Q poke chipped' (spikes[1]), 'Soak your Q poke with passive sustain and saplings' (wants.foe[1]), 'His sapling poke and passive healing' (whys[3]). Sapling Toss has no heal - its flags are knockup, slow and zone. All of Maokai's sustain is Sap Magic.
audit.why: It points the reader at the wrong ability to play around. Saplings are a zoning and vision tool on an 18s cooldown; the heal is on his autos and is accelerated by being hit with spells. Those call for completely different responses.
audit.corrected: Attribute the sustain to Sap Magic throughout.

audit.why: The packet flags 'never names any of Maokai's abilities'. The slot letters were at least all correct - W really is the root-dash and Q really is the knockback - so this was a naming gap rather than a mechanical error, unlike the Lillia entry where the slots themselves were wrong. I have put the real names in wherever an edit touched the text.

edits.before: This is his lane. His sapling and passive sustain eat your Q poke faster than you can stack it, so the chip damage that should snowball just resets every wave. At 6 his W dash plus Q knockback is a guaranteed pick if your E is down — and a tank does not care about a single root the way a squishy would. Your W barrier eats projectiles, but Maokai's threats are a dash and a melee knockback, not projectiles, so it gives you almost nothing here. Farm at max range, ping for jungle, and only commit if you catch him with W on cooldown.
edits.after: This is his lane. Sap Magic's heal cooldown drops every time one of your spells strikes him, and Radiant Volley ticks repeatedly, so the chip that should snowball just refills him each wave. At 6 his W dash plus Q knockback is a guaranteed pick if your E is down — and a tank does not care about a single root the way a squishy would. Rebuttal still blanks his damage and hands you the move speed to walk back out of melee, so hold it for the dash itself. Farm at max range, ping for jungle, and only commit if you catch him with W on cooldown.

edits.before: The lane settles into a stalemate. Your passive scales infinitely so you stay relevant, but Maokai becomes an unkillable frontline tank — your Overwhelm execute threshold is a fantasy against his HP and resists. Neither of you wins the 1v1: he can't burst you down, you can't kill a tank. Play for teamfight value where your R can detonate stacks across his whole team from range, and let the game be decided off the side lane rather than trying to solo him.

notes: Two findings here are worth more than the rest of the matchup put together. FIRST, the Sap Magic loop: his heal cooldown is reduced every time he is struck by an enemy spell, and Mel's Radiant Volley deals damage repeatedly inside its area, so her signature poke is the single fastest way to refill him. The entry describes the symptom ('the chip damage that should snowball just resets every wave') without ever naming the cause, which leaves the reader poking harder to fix a problem that poking causes. SECOND, whys[3] had the cooldown war exactly backwards - it claims 'his W is up far more often than your E', but Twisted Advance is 14/13/12/11/10 and Solar Snare is 11/10.5/10/9.5/9. Her root is faster at every rank, which flips the advice from hoarding to holding-with-confidence. Nature's Grasp appears nowhere in either layer despite being the reason an immobile mage dies here rather than merely losing; I added it to the cooldown list and the late text. Same structural blockers as the rest of my slice: full-layer diff/tone/diffRating/carryRating and every phases[N].side are under the applier's 12-char floor, so the difficulty labels cannot be corrected by proposal. I left content.win[] alone here - 'Skill' then Maokai through first item then 'Skill' is a fair reading of the kit and I had only 5 games of data, which is not enough to justify moving a chart.
